book_b.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (Harry Potter, #7)

sample_reviews.review_text:
Short and Sweet Review, by Michelle: 
 Ahh, all good things must come to an end. I am a Harry Potter nut. Why the three stars then? Well, I don't know to be honest with you. I "liked it", but I just don't know if I can go further than that. Maybe 3.5 stars? What really ruined the book for me was the epilogue. Had Ms. Rowling not included the epilogue, I think I could have gone with 4 stars. It just felt so cheesy after all the darkness that we've experienced throughout the development of the story. 
 Eh, well, I think that's all I really need to say. I highly doubt someone is scouring reviews of Harry Potter to decide if they're going to read it or not. ;) So I'll keep in short & sweet, per usual!

I think this book is a good representation of the series as a whole, charming characters, great story, and a setting that is very well crafted. I am sad that this series is over and I won't complain if more eventually are written (whether with old characters or a new generation or a mix of both) but if that happens or not I think this story's ending was absolutely perfect. I can't recommend this book and the series enough, it is just really incredible. 
 Just a quick note, Peeves has easily the best assist in the battle. (Wouldn't mind a Peeves prequel story, you know before being a ghost, just an idea...could be good...I mean really good)
I was probably the last of my generation to read this book. It's fantastic. I cried and books don't ever make me cry. Stayed up all night reading it like a little kid. Whatever.

This is the seventh and final book of the Harry Potter series. I loved this book. I thought it was well written and really fun to read. I wanted to read as quickly as I could but also slow down and enjoy it as it's the last one. When I finished, I felt like my best friend had left me. 
 This was one of the better books in the series. I love them all but this one tied up all the loose ends and really kept me enthralled. I was afraid that it would seem odd when I found out that Harry, Ron, and Hermione weren't going back to Hogwarts, but I was pleasantly surprised. Rowling kept the feel of "Harry Potter" throughout. 
 Some people were upset by the Epilogue, thinking that it was gratuitous. I can see where they are coming from but I, personally, enjoyed it. I thought it was nice to finally see Harry have a happy, normal ending. He spent the first 17 years of his life in an uproar, nothing was easy for him, he was constantly in danger. It was nice to know that, in the end, he lived a normal, calm life. 
 I thought this was a great ending to the series. It was highly suspenseful and entertaining. I loved it.

2017 reread. I remember being disappointed in this ending. It was worth 3 stars then, and I'm giving it 4 now. 
 I think the difference is me, and what point in life I read it. Some fundamental issues I had with the book were more about me, my life experiences at the time, and I was fairly exhausted and impatient generally in 2007. 
 For example, I hated the Dumbledore scenes, but now I don't. I hated the resolution, and now I don't. Maybe I've just had time to sit with the ideas, or maybe the straight through reread made it so much deeper for me. I'm not sure. 
 I still feel it's unevenly paced, and I do wish there had been equal time to the last half of the book as the first. I wish we could have seen more of Hogwarts, had a clue what was going on with DA and Snape. The wand stuff really seems spotty, still. But generally, it's a much more satisfying resolution to the story than I remember. 
 On to The Cursed Child!
Sad that the series is ending, happy because Voldy is gone, and estatic that Ron and Hermione and Harry and Ginny get together. It's all mixed feelings.

give me back my life damnit, I could have done without 500 pages of the book. Wish I had gone with my initial instinct and just checked for a detailed synopsis. Thank goodness for the couple of scenes that did end up finishing the series nicely, but give me lloyd alexander any day over this. The series would have been much better if 5,6, and 7 had been consolidated into one reasonably sized book.
Re-read December 2016
Rating 2.5 (Please don't flame me)
First HP book (and first book) I read because I thought it was the 6th book, and I watched the 5th film.

reference_book.review_text:

book_b.title: The Titan's Curse (Percy Jackson and the Olympians, #3)

sample_reviews.review_text:
Better than the second, but still pushing jokes that aren't very funny and a bit contrived. The action was fun near the end as Riordan brought in some mythological characters that I had forgotten about. The parallels to Harry Potter are almost unforgivable.... 
 I think I'll finish the series even though halfway through I thought for sure this was going to be my last. I'm glad the action picked up at the end.

This book very much follows the formula established by its predecessors even though the action is more intense, and you certainly get the feeling that author Rick Riordan is building towards his big finale. I feel like this book easily holds up to the two previous installments, but I found myself a bit underwhelmed by certain aspects, namely the formulaic feel of the beginning of the book, and Percy's serious and multiple blunders early on. On the other hand, the introduction of new characters: gods, heroes and mythical creatures alike combined with the evident path towards the true climax of the series kept me interested and made for an overall pleasant read. 
 The story starts off as the usual, almost repetitive form, with Percy answering a distress call from Grover, but this time the differences are that it's mid-winter instead of the beginning of the school year, and Annabeth and Thalia join Percy from the start. I should mention that, at this point, I began feeling very frustrated about Percy's behavior; it seemed to me that he was trying to compete with Thalia, since she is the new deal, daughter of one of The Three and all, but he is failing miserably! He is making a lot of rash and quite frankly stupid judgement calls just to prove a point to Thalia. And speaking of Thalia, it still felt weird having her back in action so suddenly, but I quickly got used to her and grew to like her a lot. Soon enough they return to Camp Half-Blood and a quest is presented, as always. As usual, there is a limited time frame to accomplish the quest. 
 Now don't get me wrong, plenty of things surprised me along the way.There is a much bigger part of the story involving gods, both new ones and the ones we've met before. Regarding the later, we get new and interesting details on them. Arthemis and her Hunters were a highlight and a really gobbled up the scenes that they were in. I loved how the gods fit together into the plot as a whole and it's always neat to see them in their updated or modernized personas. As always, the writing style is simple and to the point, and while a first person narrative from a 14 year old boy isn't very lyrical or groundbreaking, it does make for a quick and fun read. 
 Interesting quotes that I didn't include in the review: 
 There is always a way out for those clever enough to find it.
I just adore this series! They keep getting better and better!

This was a fun story. I really wish I had read these when they came out and I was still in junior high. This one got a little darker than the previous two which I really enjoyed. It really helped age and develop Percy as a main character. It was kind of refreshing to not have Annabeth in the group this go round but Zoe's "old fashioned" speech was a little annoying. She wasn't a bad character she had a big redeeming moment but in the end she was a little meh. Bianca and Nico were pretty interesting. I'm looking forward to seeing how Nico effects the next book and the conflict with him and Percy could be glorious. 
 4 stars. if I had read this as a kid I'd probably give it 5 stars.

This third novel in the series doesn't disappoint! We meet another goddess and her unusual yet intriguing followers, and the plot against the Olympians thickens. The main characters continue to grow and develop, like any normal humans. Yet another fast-paced and delightful read!

I really enjoy the use of Greek mythology in the book. I really believe it could spark children's interest in it and really what better time to learn about this stuff. 
 That said, there is something about this series that I just can't get into. I have no connection to Percy or any of the other characters. It's book 3 I should be feeling SOMETHING for them, hatred love adoration. But yet I feel nothing. 
 Maybe it's the nonstop action that make it a little hard to swollow. It's like this book is all about Percy running around a brief battle and then a small meeting of the gods. 
 This is one of those books that I really feel if I was 10-12 I'd love but I just can't get into them as an adult. Though I do think that the series is "Spicing" up so it might be a bit better in book 4 or 5. I'll have to wait and see.
4/-9:! can I just say that was freaking incredible!! I can't wait for the next book! <3

Surprisingly interesting, that or the author has worn my defenses down. I though the use of classic Greek mythology was somewhat better in this one - and I cared about more of the characters than I had been. I'm still not a Percy Jackson fan - the series would be better with a better focal character - there's just not that much going on in Percy's head. And I had never heard of Ophiotaurus.
This was pretty good, but not my favorite percy novel. Still, very well written as always.
My favourite book of the series so far !

book_b.title: The Battle of the Labyrinth (Percy Jackson and the Olympians, #4)

sample_reviews.review_text:
The Battle Of The Labyrinth (Percy Jackson And The Olympians #4), by Rick Riordan 
 Synopsis: Percy Jackson isn't expecting freshman orientation to be any fun. But when a mysterious mortal acquaintance appears on campus, followed by demon cheerleaders, things quickly move from bad to worse. 
 In this fourth installment of the blockbuster series, time is running out as war between the Olympians and the evil Titan lord Kronos draws near. Even the safe haven of Camp Half-Blood grows more vulnerable by the minute as Kronos's army prepares to invade its once impenetrable borders. To stop the invasion, Percy and his demigod friends must set out on a quest through the Labyrinth - a sprawling underground world with stunning surprises at every turn. 
 In A Sentence: A decent read, but I'm not feeling very wowed by this series (not yet anyway) 
 My Thoughts: At this point I admit I'm starting to just power through the series. It's a fun series that kids and young adults would really enjoy, but as an adult I don't feel as wowed as I could be. The chapter titles still pull a chuckle out of me, and there are sentences peppered throughout the story that are also pretty funny (case in point: "You hit the Lord of the Titans in the eye with a blue plastic hairbrush"). Ridiculous scenarios seem to be the main trademark of these books, which is always fun, but beyond that, the story doesn't hold a whole lot of depth. It's your typical action novels: lots of energy and a fast-paced plot, but very little depth and complexity. 
 Would I recommend this read? Of course! It's easy-going fun that doesn't require too much concentration. It's ridiculously funny in parts, and the incorporation of Greek Mythology into today's world is loads of fun to read about. Plus, it's a fast read, perfect for your next vacation. I'm starting the final book now and I'm looking forward to seeing how it ends. Happy reading!

sample_reviews.review_text:
OMG. I'm once again dumped head first into the world of Harry Potter. 
 I absolutely love how JK Rowling feeds us a bit of information and it turns out to be useful in the end. Nothing goes to waste and nothing is without purpose. GoF is more action based than it's precedents and things really go up a notch. Now, we really see the reality of being Harry Potter hit him. Before this, while it isn't always nice, it's a lot of fanfare and roses. I saw this thing on Tumble saying how in books 1-3, Harry is all like 'Fuck yeah! I'm Harry Potter!' and in books 4-6, he's like 'Fuck, I'm Harry Potter.' HHahahhaa that's really accurate.
Reread December 2016. Still as exciting and heartbreaking and incredible as ever.

I know a lot of people that think this book is one of the worst of the series. Worst being a loosely used term considering it's Harry Potter. Kind of like how Temple of Doom is considered the worst Indiana Jones movie, but it's still awesome because it's Indiana Jones. Anyway, those people are insane in the membrane. 
 Goblet of Fire is where things start to get truly awesome. The first three books in the series follow a pretty rigid formula: pre-Hogwarts -> at Hogwarts -> Malfoy is annoy/classes are almost a sidenote -> harry & co find out something sinister is going on -> investigation while dealing with quidditch worries -> reveal -> Harry stops Voldemort from coming back -> everyone smiles. Goblet of Fire, while loosely following that same formula, breaks free of the restrictions and does something different. Quidditch is replaced with the Triwizard tournament and sh!t is just straight cray-cray for Harry. There has never been so much mystery in one of the books prior. Who put Harry's name into the Goblet of Fire? What's Snape's real deal? Can Dumbledore be any more freaking awesome!? 
 This book turns the whole series on its head. In the first three books, Voldemort is nothing more than an insubstantial idea that the whole wizarding world is afraid of. Now he's back and ready to wreak some more havoc. Goblet of Fire is the turning point in both the series and Harry's life as a young wizard. From here on out he knows (even though he doesn't truly learn his destiny just yet) that the only reason he's alive is to stop Voldemort. While it's not really discussed, once Harry sees Voldemort rise again, he takes it as a personal challenge to avenge his parents and all the lives that were destroyed during Voldemort's previous reign of terror. 
 In my personal opinion, this is the best book in the series for all those reason. Even after reading it for the ninth time, I still love flying through the Triwizard Tournament with Harry and still get choked up when Dumbledore salutes Cedric Diggory at the end. F**cking epic!

** spoiler alert ** 
 Book 4 was definately a great one. It's the first time you get the sense that the characters are really starting to grow up. With the dance, and the Tri-Wizard competition and all. It also felt a lot more adult becuase it's the first book in the series where someone actually dies.
Emiri: 2007
Yes.

Sorting through books while unpacking, I realized I have two copies of this and OOTP in paperback. Hey, I can use this book for some of the paper crafts I've seen on Pinterest! Awesome. 
 Let me just flip through it to look at the illustra-oh, I love this part. 
 Two days later, I'd finished the re-read. 
 It's like a sickness.
Absolutely loved this book and I have to say, probably my favorite of the series so far. Mysterious, exhilarating, and overall just extraordinary - this book will keep you wanting more!

Incredible. J.K. Rowling is a master storyteller, I was shocked,scared,sad,happy,angry throughout this whole book. Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire begins the darker side of the Harry Potter books. It is the transitioning book out of middlegrade/children's books and into a older more adult series. It slowed down for me in the middle of the book between the Quidditch World Cup and the actual begining of the Triwizard Tournament but it picked back up the pace and the last 200 pages will keep you on the edge of your seat. This was the first Harry Potter book that made me cry but I know that it won't be the last. Amazing if you haven't read this series yet go get the books and read them they are more than worth it.
Amazing!! There is so much in this book that wasn't in the movie. Definitely better than the movie!

sample_reviews.review_text:
I'm so sad that these books are finished with. But I'm also very glad they have a spin off. I must say, these books are well written and action packed literally from page 1. I'm just so in love with these books. 
 Annabeth&Percy<3

As this is the last book of the series, I didn't feel there were much new development but is a satisfying end to the series. There are tense battles that see Percy and the half bloods do their best to defend Olympus from the invading armies of Kronos. We also find out more about Rachael Elizabeth Dare as well as the back stories of Luke and Annabeth. Every friend and foe that Percy has met before makes an appearance and great to see how the Titans are reimagined in this story.

Me siento tan vacia, me di todo el tiempo del mundo porque sabia que esto iba a pasar, iba a querer mas y mas aun sabiendo que todo fue perfecto y sobrepaso todos los limites. 
 Adore este libro porque simplemente estuvo tan lleno de accion y tantos plot twists que aveces quedaba en shock. Fue el desenlace perfecto.

This is an awesome series, I love it! The Titan's Curse and Battle of the Labyrinth are still my most favourites in the series. 
 This one was more serious than the other books in the series. I love Rick's writing style and storytelling. It's so fun, funny, and just awesome. This is what I mean when I say I want a good end of series battle, not like what happened in Breaking Dawn. There are many similarities between this series and HP, but they're both very good and unique as well. Although (please don't hate me), I like PJO a little bit more than I like the HP series. 
 I will be reading The Lost Hero soon, finally, now I'll understand why fans ship Jason with a brick (Brason) and what they mean by it (it's all over instagram and tumblr, altough I don't have a tumblr account, I just go there sometimes).

 My twitter account: @NazishTVDSwift 
 My Instagram accounts: @nazishreads, @nrcharmed01, and @nrtvshows 
 And I also have a facebook fan page for my blog.

Wow! The Last Olympians was amazing! There are hardly any words to describe it. Rick Riordan did an amazing job! I didn't expect any of it, there were surprises throughout the whole book! I can't imagine how any sane person could give it less than a five star rating. Anyone who reads this will absolutely love it. 
 There were some interesting turns with Percy. Also, we got to learn a lot about Luke, which was really cool. I've always liked him. I wish he could've stayed at Camp Half-Blood. And, finally, Annabeth and Percy got together. The whole book was a battle. It was brilliantly executed! 
 We lost some really lovable characters but a lot of cool things happened that made up for it. I can hardly see how anyone couldn't like The Last Olympian. There's so much information in this book about past things that have happened that pertain to this story line. It was mind blowing.
I had never felt this feeling of sadness because a series is over. A beautiful ending, I LOVED IT!!

(4.5) 
 This was definitely my favourite book of the series, it was a really good finale and Rick Riordan did a amazing job wrapping up the story and the characters. This book was filled with action from start to finish that made it a quick read and hard to put down and like all the Percy Jackson books I just had so much fun reading it. 
 I can't wait to get around to reading the Heroes of Olypmus series now.

Although there were a few times, throughout the series, where the content was a little slow to me, overall I enjoyed this series. The finale delivered with action, a few surprises and a bit of romance. The ending was a perfect finish to the series. I look forward to the first movie out in theaters next month!
Reread. Actual rating : 4.75/5

sample_reviews.review_text:
Fourth Time: 
 Started: 8/14/2016 
 Finished: 8/18/2016

** spoiler alert ** 
 **This review is for personal purposes only** 
 This is my least favorite of the HP novels. It takes what I didn't not like about Chamber of Secrets (all the unfair doubt of Harry when he knows the truth)and magnifies it with teenage angst. I thought the plot concept was the weakest of any of the books so far - at least the twist of Ginny being controlled by Voldemort in the Chamber of Secrets was fun and unexpected. It was sad that Sirius died, but I didn't feel much of a connection to him in this book as when he showed up at the end of the 3rd book. I didn't like that he was so focused on just being Harry's friend. I also disliked the plot-line of finding out how cruel Sirius and James were - it ended up ruining their characters for me. Even Lily did not come off great in this novel seeing as she married James after seeing his former behavior. I thought the Occlumency could have been better used, instead of just having Harry give up on closing off his mind and that is what leads him to the Ministry. He should have been tested with it when Voldemort showed up and learned to overcome it. Instead (as you find out in the 6th) Voldemort just blocks him off instead and all those lessons were pointless. 
 One of the few things I did like about this book were the women. Hermione handles Harry so well by being both understanding and firm with him. Ginny also blossomed into a real character this time, instead of just being Ron's shy sister who has a crush on Harry. You find out that she is both funny and fiery, taking notes from both the twins and Ron. And finally, Luna is introduced, who I love. I feel like she really adds a special element to the series. 
 The other part I love about the Order of the Phoenix is Dumbledore's Army. I wish this group would have continued into the 6th book, instead of putting the pressure back on Harry to do all the work. 
 Overall, I hate reading this book. It makes me feel tense from all the anger and angst Harry feels and the plot-line does not feel satisfying. I'll probably skip over it in the future.

I am baffled that this series is so popular. While I think the character qualities have some merit, it is just so terribly written, drawn out, and boring. There are some interesting imaginary things, but what happens with all of them--that is, the plot--stinks. Not to mention, each book is successively darker and sadder than the one which came before. For me, that indicates a dark supernatural power in it far more than the witchcraft and sorcery. Perhaps it is merely the power of good advertising. That is the only reason we know about Jackson Pollack, after all.
:D
Re-read this after finishing Half-Blood Prince, it's one star better than I originally ranked it.

Reread. I'm still not sure if this or Azkaban is my favorite. I cried just as much as I did when I was 13 and it came out, if not more. 
 Reread Sept 2017. Finished on the way to Vegas, and I only cried during Harry's conversation with Nearly Headless Nick.

As much as I love Rowling, I didn't enjoy this book as much as I would've wanted to. I also started this book in December then due to school I wasn't able to pick it back up again until June making it a little hard to get back into the groove of reading this book. I felt as though the book moved along slowly for me and it didn't start picking up until the last 6 chapters, where I found myself unable to put the book down until I finished it. If I had that feeling during the beginning or even during the halfway point of the book then I would have easily given this book a 4 out of 5 or even a 5 out of 5. Instead, due to the slow lag I could only give the book a 3. Also, Harry's attitude was slightly annoying to me as well during the middle half of the book. He would get angry and yell and just plainly be rude with the only people willing to help him in a dire situation. I love Luna Lovegood and wished that she was more prominent in this book. Hopefully, she'll get more shine as the series progresses.

Harry Potter... Well, I'm not that big of a fan, but my friends said I have to finish the series before the last move comes out. So I FINALLY finished this one on my way back from Arizona. Rowling is such an amazing writer, with so much description. It just takes me SOOO long to read 870 pages.
Just love this series solo much! Not my favorite of the seven but always worth reading :)

sample_reviews.review_text:
OMG. I'm once again dumped head first into the world of Harry Potter. 
 I absolutely love how JK Rowling feeds us a bit of information and it turns out to be useful in the end. Nothing goes to waste and nothing is without purpose. GoF is more action based than it's precedents and things really go up a notch. Now, we really see the reality of being Harry Potter hit him. Before this, while it isn't always nice, it's a lot of fanfare and roses. I saw this thing on Tumble saying how in books 1-3, Harry is all like 'Fuck yeah! I'm Harry Potter!' and in books 4-6, he's like 'Fuck, I'm Harry Potter.' HHahahhaa that's really accurate.
Reread December 2016. Still as exciting and heartbreaking and incredible as ever.

I know a lot of people that think this book is one of the worst of the series. Worst being a loosely used term considering it's Harry Potter. Kind of like how Temple of Doom is considered the worst Indiana Jones movie, but it's still awesome because it's Indiana Jones. Anyway, those people are insane in the membrane. 
 Goblet of Fire is where things start to get truly awesome. The first three books in the series follow a pretty rigid formula: pre-Hogwarts -> at Hogwarts -> Malfoy is annoy/classes are almost a sidenote -> harry & co find out something sinister is going on -> investigation while dealing with quidditch worries -> reveal -> Harry stops Voldemort from coming back -> everyone smiles. Goblet of Fire, while loosely following that same formula, breaks free of the restrictions and does something different. Quidditch is replaced with the Triwizard tournament and sh!t is just straight cray-cray for Harry. There has never been so much mystery in one of the books prior. Who put Harry's name into the Goblet of Fire? What's Snape's real deal? Can Dumbledore be any more freaking awesome!? 
 This book turns the whole series on its head. In the first three books, Voldemort is nothing more than an insubstantial idea that the whole wizarding world is afraid of. Now he's back and ready to wreak some more havoc. Goblet of Fire is the turning point in both the series and Harry's life as a young wizard. From here on out he knows (even though he doesn't truly learn his destiny just yet) that the only reason he's alive is to stop Voldemort. While it's not really discussed, once Harry sees Voldemort rise again, he takes it as a personal challenge to avenge his parents and all the lives that were destroyed during Voldemort's previous reign of terror. 
 In my personal opinion, this is the best book in the series for all those reason. Even after reading it for the ninth time, I still love flying through the Triwizard Tournament with Harry and still get choked up when Dumbledore salutes Cedric Diggory at the end. F**cking epic!

** spoiler alert ** 
 Book 4 was definately a great one. It's the first time you get the sense that the characters are really starting to grow up. With the dance, and the Tri-Wizard competition and all. It also felt a lot more adult becuase it's the first book in the series where someone actually dies.

Absolutely loved this book and I have to say, probably my favorite of the series so far. Mysterious, exhilarating, and overall just extraordinary - this book will keep you wanting more!

Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire begins the darker side of the Harry Potter books. It is the transitioning book out of middlegrade/children's books and into a older more adult series. It slowed down for me in the middle of the book between the Quidditch World Cup and the actual begining of the Triwizard Tournament but it picked back up the pace and the last 200 pages will keep you on the edge of your seat. This was the first Harry Potter book that made me cry but I know that it won't be the last. Amazing if you haven't read this series yet go get the books and read them they are more than worth it.
Amazing!! There is so much in this book that wasn't in the movie. Definitely better than the movie!

book_b.title: The Last Olympian (Percy Jackson and the Olympians, #5)

sample_reviews.review_text:
I'm so sad that these books are finished with. But I'm also very glad they have a spin off. I must say, these books are well written and action packed literally from page 1. I'm just so in love with these books. 
 Annabeth&Percy<3

As this is the last book of the series, I didn't feel there were much new development but is a satisfying end to the series. There are tense battles that see Percy and the half bloods do their best to defend Olympus from the invading armies of Kronos. We also find out more about Rachael Elizabeth Dare as well as the back stories of Luke and Annabeth. Every friend and foe that Percy has met before makes an appearance and great to see how the Titans are reimagined in this story.

Me siento tan vacia, me di todo el tiempo del mundo porque sabia que esto iba a pasar, iba a querer mas y mas aun sabiendo que todo fue perfecto y sobrepaso todos los limites. 
 Adore este libro porque simplemente estuvo tan lleno de accion y tantos plot twists que aveces quedaba en shock. Fue el desenlace perfecto.

This is an awesome series, I love it! The Titan's Curse and Battle of the Labyrinth are still my most favourites in the series. 
 This one was more serious than the other books in the series. I love Rick's writing style and storytelling. It's so fun, funny, and just awesome. This is what I mean when I say I want a good end of series battle, not like what happened in Breaking Dawn. There are many similarities between this series and HP, but they're both very good and unique as well. Although (please don't hate me), I like PJO a little bit more than I like the HP series. 
 I will be reading The Lost Hero soon, finally, now I'll understand why fans ship Jason with a brick (Brason) and what they mean by it (it's all over instagram and tumblr, altough I don't have a tumblr account, I just go there sometimes). 
 My book blog: nazishreads.net 
 My twitter account: @NazishTVDSwift 
 My Instagram accounts: @nazishreads, @nrcharmed01, and @nrtvshows 
 And I also have a facebook fan page for my blog.

Wow! The Last Olympians was amazing! There are hardly any words to describe it. Rick Riordan did an amazing job! I didn't expect any of it, there were surprises throughout the whole book! I can't imagine how any sane person could give it less than a five star rating. Anyone who reads this will absolutely love it. 
 There were some interesting turns with Percy. Also, we got to learn a lot about Luke, which was really cool. I've always liked him. I wish he could've stayed at Camp Half-Blood. And, finally, Annabeth and Percy got together. The whole book was a battle. It was brilliantly executed! 
 We lost some really lovable characters but a lot of cool things happened that made up for it. I can hardly see how anyone couldn't like The Last Olympian. There's so much information in this book about past things that have happened that pertain to this story line. It was mind blowing.
I had never felt this feeling of sadness because a series is over. A beautiful ending, I LOVED IT!!

(4.5) 
 This was definitely my favourite book of the series, it was a really good finale and Rick Riordan did a amazing job wrapping up the story and the characters. This book was filled with action from start to finish that made it a quick read and hard to put down and like all the Percy Jackson books I just had so much fun reading it. 
 I can't wait to get around to reading the Heroes of Olypmus series now.

Although there were a few times, throughout the series, where the content was a little slow to me, overall I enjoyed this series. The finale delivered with action, a few surprises and a bit of romance. The ending was a perfect finish to the series. I look forward to the first movie out in theaters next month!
Reread. Actual rating : 4.75/5

book_a.title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)

sample_reviews.review_text: This book is amazing! It seriously keeps you involved the whole time and there are several different villains to keep your eye on!

** spoiler alert ** 
 **This review is for personal purposes only** 
 This is my least favorite of the HP novels. It takes what I didn't not like about Chamber of Secrets (all the unfair doubt of Harry when he knows the truth)and magnifies it with teenage angst. I thought the plot concept was the weakest of any of the books so far - at least the twist of Ginny being controlled by Voldemort in the Chamber of Secrets was fun and unexpected. It was sad that Sirius died, but I didn't feel much of a connection to him in this book as when he showed up at the end of the 3rd book. I didn't like that he was so focused on just being Harry's friend. I also disliked the plot-line of finding out how cruel Sirius and James were - it ended up ruining their characters for me. Even Lily did not come off great in this novel seeing as she married James after seeing his former behavior. I thought the Occlumency could have been better used, instead of just having Harry give up on closing off his mind and that is what leads him to the Ministry. He should have been tested with it when Voldemort showed up and learned to overcome it. Instead (as you find out in the 6th) Voldemort just blocks him off instead and all those lessons were pointless. 
 One of the few things I did like about this book were the women. Hermione handles Harry so well by being both understanding and firm with him. Ginny also blossomed into a real character this time, instead of just being Ron's shy sister who has a crush on Harry. You find out that she is both funny and fiery, taking notes from both the twins and Ron. And finally, Luna is introduced, who I love. I feel like she really adds a special element to the series. 
 The other part I love about the Order of the Phoenix is Dumbledore's Army. I wish this group would have continued into the 6th book, instead of putting the pressure back on Harry to do all the work. 
 Overall, I hate reading this book. It makes me feel tense from all the anger and angst Harry feels and the plot-line does not feel satisfying. I'll probably skip over it in the future.

I am baffled that this series is so popular. While I think the character qualities have some merit, it is just so terribly written, drawn out, and boring. There are some interesting imaginary things, but what happens with all of them--that is, the plot--stinks. Not to mention, each book is successively darker and sadder than the one which came before. For me, that indicates a dark supernatural power in it far more than the witchcraft and sorcery. Perhaps it is merely the power of good advertising.  All this is old news, but I re-read most of The Order of The Phoenix over the holidays, just because I like it so much. And also because I appreciate its brief but gentle treatment of mental illness. 
 My absolute favorite scene is when Neville, a minor character, realizes his friends know that his parents are mentally ill. His bossy grandmother is there, and she tells him what to do and how to feel. But Neville takes his own approach, which is shyer, sweeter and in the end much more courageous. 
 Another wonderful minor character was the socially awkward Luna Lovegood. My favorite scene with her is at the very end of the book, when Harry stumbles onto Luna in the hall on the last day of the term. At first he wants to hide from her. Then, when he realizes that she knows how odd she seems to everyone else, he feels sorry for her. By the time he walks away, he is very glad to have talked to her. 
 I thought it was sad when Luna told Harry that their schoolmates played tricks on her. Bret disagreed. "She wasn't sad about it," he said. "She was handling it just fine." 
 And she was--which may explain why her strangeness is so likable. 
 She and the clumsy but determined Neville are the reasons I've read Harry Potter 5 more than once.

sample_reviews.review_text:
Short and Sweet Review, by Michelle: 
 Ahh, all good things must come to an end. I am a Harry Potter nut. Why the three stars then? Well, I don't know to be honest with you. I "liked it", but I just don't know if I can go further than that. Maybe 3.5 stars? What really ruined the book for me was the epilogue. Had Ms. Rowling not included the epilogue, I think I could have gone with 4 stars. It just felt so cheesy after all the darkness that we've experienced throughout the development of the story. 
 Eh, well, I think that's all I really need to say. I highly doubt someone is scouring reviews of Harry Potter to decide if they're going to read it or not. ;) So I'll keep in short & sweet, per usual!
Amazing!!!
I was probably the last of my generation to read this book. It's fantastic. I cried and books don't ever make me cry. Stayed up all night reading it like a little kid. Whatever.

Bittersweet Book. It is an amazing and emotional conclusion to the journey we started 7 years prior. Sadly, we must let go of the characters, at least for now. Rowling brings in the epic-ness for one final showdown. No one is forgotten. Every character gets some form of a conclusion, only leaving questions for us fangirls/boys about their futures beyond. This is by the best of the series. Full 5 out of 5 stars, although should be more in possible. Nothing more to say, other than, if you haven't read this series yet, why are you reading this, go now, in any way you choose, discover the wonderful world of Harry Potter.

2017 reread. I remember being disappointed in this ending. It was worth 3 stars then, and I'm giving it 4 now. 
 I think the difference is me, and what point in life I read it. Some fundamental issues I had with the book were more about me, my life experiences at the time, and I was fairly exhausted and impatient generally in 2007. 
 For example, I hated the Dumbledore scenes, but now I don't. I hated the resolution, and now I don't. Maybe I've just had time to sit with the ideas, or maybe the straight through reread made it so much deeper for me. I'm not sure. 
 I still feel it's unevenly paced, and I do wish there had been equal time to the last half of the book as the first. I wish we could have seen more of Hogwarts, had a clue what was going on with DA and Snape. The wand stuff really seems spotty, still. But generally, it's a much more satisfying resolution to the story than I remember. 
 On to The Cursed Child!
Sad that the series is ending, happy because Voldy is gone, and estatic that Ron and Hermione and Harry and Ginny get together. It's all mixed feelings.

give me back my life damnit, I could have done without 500 pages of the book. Wish I had gone with my initial instinct and just checked for a detailed synopsis. Thank goodness for the couple of scenes that did end up finishing the series nicely, but give me lloyd alexander any day over this. The series would have been much better if 5,6, and 7 had been consolidated into one reasonably sized book.

This book was brilliant, I just couldn't stop reading!

sample_reviews.review_text: This book is amazing! It seriously keeps you involved the whole time and there are several different villains to keep your eye on!

** spoiler alert ** 
 **This review is for personal purposes only** 
 This is my least favorite of the HP novels. It takes what I didn't not like about Chamber of Secrets (all the unfair doubt of Harry when he knows the truth)and magnifies it with teenage angst. I thought the plot concept was the weakest of any of the books so far - at least the twist of Ginny being controlled by Voldemort in the Chamber of Secrets was fun and unexpected. It was sad that Sirius died, but I didn't feel much of a connection to him in this book as when he showed up at the end of the 3rd book. I didn't like that he was so focused on just being Harry's friend. I also disliked the plot-line of finding out how cruel Sirius and James were - it ended up ruining their characters for me. Even Lily did not come off great in this novel seeing as she married James after seeing his former behavior. I thought the Occlumency could have been better used, instead of just having Harry give up on closing off his mind and that is what leads him to the Ministry. He should have been tested with it when Voldemort showed up and learned to overcome it. Instead (as you find out in the 6th) Voldemort just blocks him off instead and all those lessons were pointless. 
 One of the few things I did like about this book were the women. Hermione handles Harry so well by being both understanding and firm with him. Ginny also blossomed into a real character this time, instead of just being Ron's shy sister who has a crush on Harry. You find out that she is both funny and fiery, taking notes from both the twins and Ron. And finally, Luna is introduced, who I love. I feel like she really adds a special element to the series. 
 The other part I love about the Order of the Phoenix is Dumbledore's Army. I wish this group would have continued into the 6th book, instead of putting the pressure back on Harry to do all the work. 
 Overall, I hate reading this book. It makes me feel tense from all the anger and angst Harry feels and the plot-line does not feel satisfying. I'll probably skip over it in the future.

I am baffled that this series is so popular. While I think the character qualities have some merit, it is just so terribly written, drawn out, and boring. There are some interesting imaginary things, but what happens with all of them--that is, the plot--stinks. Not to mention, each book is successively darker and sadder than the one which came before. For me, that indicates a dark supernatural power in it far more than the witchcraft and sorcery. Perhaps it is merely the power of good advertising. That is the only reason we know about Jackson Pollack, after all.
:D

I didn't like all of the anger and angst in the first 200 pages. All it was about Harry throwing an inner (and outwardly, too) tantrum and whining. I didn't believe it all to be in character, but we all act like that at some point in our lives. I also hated the death of Sirius. I know that his death was to make a point: that Harry must ultimately face Voldemort alone. I still mourned the loss of Sirius, he was my favorite character. I wish he had a bigger part in Harry's life and within the series.
Not a reread!! Still amazing!! Loved all the humor and the spells!! Only two books left!! :(

Malfoy always taunts Harry, Ron, and Hermione. Snape always hates Harry and the Griffyndors for no apparent reason, and his bias is never questioned. Lee Jordan always swears at the Quidditch matches and gets scolded by McGonnogal. Harry always manages to barely catch the snitch just in time to win a Quidditch match for Gryffindor. Harry and Ron always suck at classes while Hermione gets shamed for doing well. 
 See how I revealed no spoilers there? 
 There's only so much of the same thing you can read over and over again before it all blends together into a boring mess. Five books of this?! With the plot drawn out for hundreds of useless pages? Why would I want to endure three ignorant teenagers complaining about not being told anything, while they whisper secrets in the open and lazily sit by watching the action go on around them? Why can't I be in on the big-kids' table, and help the adults put things together? While reading this I constantly had to ask myself... How are these good characters again? There's something wrong when the two-dimensional side characters are more intriguing than your three musketeers. 
 Hmm, I wonder why it's so hard to ignore the school bully long enough, so you can keep playing your favorite sport, Harry? 
 Hmm, it must be hard to control a conversation long enough to say what you want to your own godfather, Harry. 
 Hmm, so you want to "burn" the useful gift your brilliant friend gave you for help, Harry? You and your best friend pay no attention when Hermione, the successful student, tries to help your study schedule (never thought that might help you become an Auror, did you, Harry?). That must have something to do with the fact that you haven't yet realized how reading actually helps in real life, dear Harry. 
 Hmm, I wonder why it's a bad idea your mind is linked with Voldemort's, Harry. 
 Hmm, could it be a good idea to guard your mind from your worst enemy, Harry? 
 Hmm, how about you stop complaining and learn from the people you envy or criticize, Harry? 
 Please tell me why anyone would like reading 600 pages of dull plot surrounding this guy's attitude problems? I don't get it. 
 The only new material in this one is Umbridge's infernal presence, which was entertaining. But Rowling took 800+ pages to retell the same story she's done four times before, inserting maybe 20% new material, while boring me with the rest of the useless rambling junk. Stop killing so many trees and use less of my time. Stop asking so many questions, and make something actually happen. Stop writing about hormonal teenager problems, and give me morality and suspense. Give fewer homework troubles to your idiot main character, and describe more of the legacy behind everything actually driving this plot. Stop feeding me the same patronizing slop... I can see through it. 
 At least the last 200 pages are interesting. 
 Why are all the side characters seemingly more interesting than the protagonist? It's because Rowling refuses to actually use the entire 800 pages for character development. Instead she crams all the good action into the last 5-7 chapters (making me guilty for feeling happy, after struggling through the slothful 600 previous pages). 
 This book earns 3 stars only for Rowling's inventive creations in the wizarding world, and the last 7 chapters which made the whole 800+ pages of drudgery somewhat worth it. But when the environment is more interesting than the plot... Errrrr... There's a problem. 
 I'm sorry, but if you've failed to make your hero interesting by the fifth book, just stop... stop using your international fame to put me through this mediocre excuse for a saga... It was interesting in book one, Rowling, because that one was 200 pages. And maybe you could pass it by me again in book two. But no more... Please no eighth book... Please, I'm begging you... 
 *sigh* Now on to book six: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince. I'm gonna guess that the next 800+ pages have more of the same idiotic lines from Ron that pass for quality children's literature...

I actually finished this book over a month ago, but the mobile app somehow didn't sync w/ the website. Ah, well... 
 Still a good read, although it's always the hardest one for me to get through.

So Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince is my least favorite HP movie, so I was pleasantly surprised that the book is a lot better. Even though, I kinda missed the whole deatheaters scene at the Burrow during Christmas, it was still way better. I throughly enjoyed this!
Another excellent re-read of a favourite.
For the love of all things holy ... WHY IS THIS BOOK SO LONG? WHERE ARE THE EDITORS WITH THE BRIGHT RED PENS? I could have taken 150+ pages off this thing easily.
At the end of the series, everything became much more serious. The magic disappeared, and I missed that.

Wow! Holy crap!!! I just read this book in two days, I couldn't put it down, and that's quite a feat having two small children! This is now my favorite book of the series. Way better than the movie. The book explains so much more about Voldemort's life that I understand him now as a character, his strengths and weaknesses. Character development and relationships are so much better explained in the book rather than the movie. I can't wait to crack open the next book! I've only seen the last movies once so I feel as if I'm going into the last book a little blind. I am so thankful I went ahead and read the books anyway because I understand way more than I ever could have just relying on the movies!
Full discussion here (with spoilers): https://cutloosebookloose.wordpress.c...

The book with the greatest potential and the greatest let down. 
 Don't get me wrong, the Harry Potter series (the first four at least) can be enchanting, engaging and a truly worthy read... 
 ... BUT it's not worth the hype. I could name HUNDREDS of books and a score of series that would be a better use of your time than HP but, sadly, did not receive the "hype" this series did. Until the last two, somewhat three, books were read, I was somewhat of a Potter nut. I gave the fourth book five stars for a reason, after all. But starting at the fifth book, the story begins to fall off track. 
 The sixth book was downright disappointing, the fact that a FAN GIRL gets the hero annoyed me, the seventh book, had it's moments, I admit but Rowling should be shot for that pathetic epilogue. I've seen better writing from ten year olds and I am not exaggerating. 
 Over all, I would tell you to try the series out. It's been a great gate-way book into other (more worthy) fantasy books for many, many people and HAS convinced many kids out there that reading can be fun! It's one of the few series out there that I believe will have some historical value because of that fact. 
 If you are looking for an astoundingly great read, however... 
 ... look elsewhere.(

I'm so sad that these books are finished with. But I'm also very glad they have a spin off. I must say, these books are well written and action packed literally from page 1. I'm just so in love with these books. 
 Annabeth&Percy<3

I kinda skimmed through the second half of it. I just thought it dragged on a little. 
 Maybe I should've reread the previous books before starting this one.

Me siento tan vacia, me di todo el tiempo del mundo porque sabia que esto iba a pasar, iba a querer mas y mas aun sabiendo que todo fue perfecto y sobrepaso todos los limites. 
 Adore este libro porque simplemente estuvo tan lleno de accion y tantos plot twists que aveces quedaba en shock. Fue el desenlace perfecto.

This is an awesome series, I love it! The Titan's Curse and Battle of the Labyrinth are still my most favourites in the series. 
 This one was more serious than the other books in the series. I love Rick's writing style and storytelling. It's so fun, funny, and just awesome. This is what I mean when I say I want a good end of series battle, not like what happened in Breaking Dawn. There are many similarities between this series and HP, but they're both very good and unique as well. Although (please don't hate me), I like PJO a little bit more than I like the HP series. 
 I will be reading The Lost Hero soon, finally, now I'll understand why fans ship Jason with a brick (Brason) and what they mean by it (it's all over instagram and tumblr, altough I don't have a tumblr account, I just go there sometimes).

 My twitter account: @NazishTVDSwift 
 My Instagram accounts: @nazishreads, @nrcharmed01, and @nrtvshows 
 And I also have a facebook fan page for my blog.

Wow! The Last Olympians was amazing! There are hardly any words to describe it. Rick Riordan did an amazing job! I didn't expect any of it, there were surprises throughout the whole book! I can't imagine how any sane person could give it less than a five star rating. Anyone who reads this will absolutely love it. 
 There were some interesting turns with Percy. Also, we got to learn a lot about Luke, which was really cool. I've always liked him. I wish he could've stayed at Camp Half-Blood. And, finally, Annabeth and Percy got together. The whole book was a battle. It was brilliantly executed! 
 We lost some really lovable characters but a lot of cool things happened that made up for it. I can hardly see how anyone couldn't like The Last Olympian. There's so much information in this book about past things that have happened that pertain to this story line. It was mind blowing.

I am so happy to be done with this book/series. It took me forever and I just could not get into it. Part of me wanted Hades to kill Percy Jackson and just get it over with! In the end the books are well written and I enjoyed them.. Who knows, I might even read the next series.
I had never felt this feeling of sadness because a series is over. A beautiful ending, I LOVED IT!!

(4.5) 
 This was definitely my favourite book of the series, it was a really good finale and Rick Riordan did a amazing job wrapping up the story and the characters. This book was filled with action from start to finish that made it a quick read and hard to put down and like all the Percy Jackson books I just had so much fun reading it. 
 I can't wait to get around to reading the Heroes of Olypmus series now.
Another one I'm sure I read but can't remember much about. Except that I really enjoyed it.
Reread. Actual rating : 4.75/5

book_b.title: The Sea of Monsters (Percy Jackson and the Olympians, #2)

sample_reviews.review_text:
It's been a year since Percy Jackson learned that he is a demigod, the son of his human mother and Poseidon, the Greek God of the sea. On his last day of school, Percy hopes to finish the year without any major disasters and head off to Camp Half Blood, a summer camp for demigods. Unfortunately, trouble has a knack for finding Percy, and he has a run-in with some monsters in gym class. Saved by his friend Annabeth and his classmate Tyson, they escape to camp. 
 Camp Half Blood is not how Percy remembers it. The protective magical boundary of camp is collapsing, monsters are invading the borders, and the camp staff has changed. To make things worse, Percy keeps having dreams about his friend Grover, a satyr on a quest, being in danger. It turns out that Grover has created and "empathy link", allowing him to communicate with Percy from a distance. Between Grover, Hermes, and the Gray Sisters, Percy pieces together clues as to how he can save Camp Half Blood, as well as Grover. Percy's latest quest will take him to the Sea of Monsters, the fabled site of creatures such as Charybdis and the Sirens. In this sequel, Percy will take on old foes and new ones, make new friends, and discover more about his father and family. 
 One of the things I love most about this series is how covertly educational it is! Percy interacts with many characters from Greek mythology and Percy often recalls a quick line or two about the story behind those characters. I recall learning about mythology in grade school and it's fun to revisit those tales. Mention is also given to the works of Greek historians, and I must give kudos to Riordan for making Homer's Odyssey seem interesting! 
 I love how you never know what's going to happen next in this series. Yes, you know something isn't going to be as easy as it initially seems, but you never know who or what to expect! Riordan has a tendency of leading the reader to feel like the worst is over, and then suddenly he throws in another unexpected element. I enjoy guessing what is coming based on context clues (e.g. in book one, when they were at Auntie Em's Garden Emporium and there were tons of horrified looking stone statues- If you know your Greek mythology, you know Medusa is coming!). 
 The only thing that drove me nuts about this book was how oblivious Percy seems to have become. In the first book, he's not well versed in mythology so Annabeth and Grover are often explaining what things are to him. If I suddenly discovered that all of those stories I'd learned in school were in fact real, I'd head home and hit the books to learn as much as I possibly could. I'd also become more aware of my surroundings. Percy, however, seems to have gone home and left his demigod self at Camp Half Blood for the year. He is fully aware of the "mist" and how it keeps humans from perceiving otherworldly things, but allows himself to be fooled by it on multiple occasions. He also requires a great deal of explanation from Annabeth regarding mythological stories. Percy has obviously never heard the quote, "Know thy enemy"! 
 This book is by no means a difficult read. It's obviously geared towards a younger crowd, but adults can definitely enjoy it as well! I'm 23, and I love what I've read thus far! I even went ahead and bought the remainder of the series! This book took me a grand total of two days to read, but part of that was because I couldn't put it down. It's well written, and you have the opportunity to learn more about the key characters and their lives, as well as gain more of the history of Camp Half Blood. 
 This second installment in the Percy Jackson series is exciting and interesting, taking the reader to many new places along the East coast of the United States. If you've got a child, or even if you enjoy a light read yourself, this book is the second installment in a series that has many great elements- adventure, mythology, action and more! Check it out!

okay...wtf did i just read??? There is nothing original in this book half of the characters are modernized gods or myths e.g Medussa and Perseus. I really dont care about the characters....who are somewhat like Harry potter but flat and not very likeable. 
 i had started to do a step by step comparison but i guess i shouldn't be too hard on him because it's a children's book. Although harry potter was a children's book and put many 'grown up' novels to shame. Perhaps i'm the only one who sees the connection. Perhaps it is fabricated in my mind but this books sucks.
A cute, entertaining read, but nothing extraordinary.
Loved it!

On his last day of school, Percy hopes to finish the year without any major disasters and head off to Camp Half Blood, a summer camp for demigods. Unfortunately, trouble has a knack for finding Percy, and he has a run-in with some monsters in gym class. Saved by his friend Annabeth and his classmate Tyson, they escape to camp. 
 Camp Half Blood is not how Percy remembers it. The protective magical boundary of camp is collapsing, monsters are invading the borders, and the camp staff has changed. To make things worse, Percy keeps having dreams about his friend Grover, a satyr on a quest, being in danger. It turns out that Grover has created and "empathy link", allowing him to communicate with Percy from a distance. Between Grover, Hermes, and the Gray Sisters, Percy pieces together clues as to how he can save Camp Half Blood, as well as Grover. Percy's latest quest will take him to the Sea of Monsters, the fabled site of creatures such as Charybdis and the Sirens. In this sequel, Percy will take on old foes and new ones, make new friends, and discover more about his father and family. 
 One of the things I love most about this series is how covertly educational it is! Percy interacts with many characters from Greek mythology and Percy often recalls a quick line or two about the story behind those characters. I recall learning about mythology in grade school and it's fun to revisit those tales. Mention is also given to the works of Greek historians, and I must give kudos to Riordan for making Homer's Odyssey seem interesting! 
 I love how you never know what's going to happen next in this series. Yes, you know something isn't going to be as easy as it initially seems, but you never know who or what to expect! Riordan has a tendency of leading the reader to feel like the worst is over, and then suddenly he throws in another unexpected element. I enjoy guessing what is coming based on context clues (e.g. in book one, when they were at Auntie Em's Garden Emporium and there were tons of horrified looking stone statues- If you know your Greek mythology, you know Medusa is coming!). 
 The only thing that drove me nuts about this book was how oblivious Percy seems to have become. In the first book, he's not well versed in mythology so Annabeth and Grover are often explaining what things are to him. If I suddenly discovered that all of those stories I'd learned in school were in fact real, I'd head home and hit the books to learn as much as I possibly could. I'd also become more aware of my surroundings. Percy, however, seems to have gone home and left his demigod self at Camp Half Blood for the year. He is fully aware of the "mist" and how it keeps humans from perceiving otherworldly things, but allows himself to be fooled by it on multiple occasions. He also requires a great deal of explanation from Annabeth regarding mythological stories. Percy has obviously never heard the quote, "Know thy enemy"! 
 This book is by no means a difficult read. It's obviously geared towards a younger crowd, but adults can definitely enjoy it as well! I'm 23, and I love what I've read thus far! I even went ahead and bought the remainder of the series! This book took me a grand total of two days to read, but part of that was because I couldn't put it down. It's well written, and you have the opportunity to learn more about the key characters and their lives, as well as gain more of the history of Camp Half Blood. 
 This second installment in the Percy Jackson series is exciting and interesting, taking the reader to many new places along the East coast of the United States. If you've got a child, or even if you enjoy a light read yourself, this book is the second installment in a series that has many great elements- adventure, mythology, action and more! Check it out!

Although harry potter was a children's book and put many 'grown up' novels to shame. Perhaps i'm the only one who sees the connection. Perhaps it is fabricated in my mind but this books sucks.

reference_book.review_text:
I finally put my finger on what I didn't like about this book. The characters! 
 Percy annoys me to no end. The author makes too many pointless attempts at humor through him, and when I say too many, I mean in every paragraph. Plus, he's whiny; I don't like whiny heroes. 
 The only decent character was Chiron. He was by far the only mature one...even the gods act like little kids. 
 And there were some holes, too...The most annoying one was Percy's Achilles Heel. There should be a rule in literature that if there is a weak point mentioned, it should be just that, a weak point. He should've at least been stabbed once...Chekhov's gun, anyone? Bathing in the River Styx wasn't anywhere near as dangerous as everyone kept implying, and at the end, it was left as an insignificant detail.

sample_reviews.review_text:
The Battle Of The Labyrinth (Percy Jackson And The Olympians #4), by Rick Riordan 
 Synopsis: Percy Jackson isn't expecting freshman orientation to be any fun. But when a mysterious mortal acquaintance appears on campus, followed by demon cheerleaders, things quickly move from bad to worse. 
 In this fourth installment of the blockbuster series, time is running out as war between the Olympians and the evil Titan lord Kronos draws near. Even the safe haven of Camp Half-Blood grows more vulnerable by the minute as Kronos's army prepares to invade its once impenetrable borders. To stop the invasion, Percy and his demigod friends must set out on a quest through the Labyrinth - a sprawling underground world with stunning surprises at every turn. 
 In A Sentence: A decent read, but I'm not feeling very wowed by this series (not yet anyway) 
 My Thoughts: At this point I admit I'm starting to just power through the series. It's a fun series that kids and young adults would really enjoy, but as an adult I don't feel as wowed as I could be. The chapter titles still pull a chuckle out of me, and there are sentences peppered throughout the story that are also pretty funny (case in point: "You hit the Lord of the Titans in the eye with a blue plastic hairbrush"). Ridiculous scenarios seem to be the main trademark of these books, which is always fun, but beyond that, the story doesn't hold a whole lot of depth. It's your typical action novels: lots of energy and a fast-paced plot, but very little depth and complexity. 
 Would I recommend this read? Of course! It's easy-going fun that doesn't require too much concentration. It's ridiculously funny in parts, and the incorporation of Greek Mythology into today's world is loads of fun to read about. Plus, it's a fast read, perfect for your next vacation. I'm starting the final book now and I'm looking forward to seeing how it ends. Happy reading!

"Don't judge someone until you've stood at his forge and worked with this hammer."

 I was so happy of seeing Rachel in this book.I just fell in love with her from the first time when she appeared in the last book.I know Percy and Annabeth will end up together and I love Annabeth very very much...But gods!Rachel and Percy would be a GREAT couple! 
 "You hit the Lord of the Titans in the eye with a blue plastic hairbrush." 
 See?How can anyone not like her?

I'm not sure what I said for the Titan's Curse by Rick Riordan, but honestly, this book is my fave so far. I can't even remember what happened in the Titan's Curse because I was just sooo intrigued by this storyline. A job well done!

** spoiler alert ** 
 I can't decide if my favorite line of the book was "I tried to talk to Annabeth, but she was acting like I'd just punched her grandmother." or "So which way now, Sacagawea?" 
 Starting out I wasn't so sure I was going to like this one any better than the last one, but after finishing I found that I was much more interested in book 4. I think the story was less predictable, and (maybe because) the formula of the story has finally changed (at least a little). 
 I did find some time-line confusions...such as Percy stating his bunk was how he left it last summer, but wasn't he there over winter? I think I caught some other things that made me raise an eyebrow, but I can't recall them. Which is fine, for I am left with having enjoyed the book and anxious for the conclusion of the series. 
 *Update* 
 After reading the first few pages of book 5 I recall how annoyed I was in the beginnings of books 3 and 4. I feel like I'm missing a huge chunk of story. Why isn't there any bridge to cover the gap between each book? How did it ever make sense to write it this way?
I thought this book was really good! It had action and fun,suspense, and had you pulled into the story! I felt like i was apart of these books!

Wow! The Last Olympians was amazing! There are hardly any words to describe it. Rick Riordan did an amazing job! I didn't expect any of it, there were surprises throughout the whole book! I can't imagine how any sane person could give it less than a five star rating. Anyone who reads this will absolutely love it. 
 There were some interesting turns with Percy. Also, we got to learn a lot about Luke, which was really cool. I've always liked him. I wish he could've stayed at Camp Half-Blood. And, finally, Annabeth and Percy got together. The whole book was a battle. It was brilliantly executed! 
 We lost some really lovable characters but a lot of cool things happened that made up for it. I can hardly see how anyone couldn't like The Last Olympian. There's so much information in this book about past things that have happened that pertain to this story line. It was mind blowing.
I had never felt this feeling of sadness because a series is over. A beautiful ending, I LOVED IT!!

(4.5)

 I can't wait to get around to reading the Heroes of Olypmus series now.

sample_reviews.review_text:
The Battle Of The Labyrinth (Percy Jackson And The Olympians #4), by Rick Riordan 
 Synopsis: Percy Jackson isn't expecting freshman orientation to be any fun. But when a mysterious mortal acquaintance appears on campus, followed by demon cheerleaders, things quickly move from bad to worse. 
 In this fourth installment of the blockbuster series, time is running out as war between the Olympians and the evil Titan lord Kronos draws near. Even the safe haven of Camp Half-Blood grows more vulnerable by the minute as Kronos's army prepares to invade its once impenetrable borders. To stop the invasion, Percy and his demigod friends must set out on a quest through the Labyrinth - a sprawling underground world with stunning surprises at every turn. 
 In A Sentence: A decent read, but I'm not feeling very wowed by this series (not yet anyway) 
 My Thoughts: At this point I admit I'm starting to just power through the series. It's a fun series that kids and young adults would really enjoy, but as an adult I don't feel as wowed as I could be. The chapter titles still pull a chuckle out of me, and there are sentences peppered throughout the story that are also pretty funny (case in point: "You hit the Lord of the Titans in the eye with a blue plastic hairbrush"). Ridiculous scenarios seem to be the main trademark of these books, which is always fun, but beyond that, the story doesn't hold a whole lot of depth. It's your typical action novels: lots of energy and a fast-paced plot, but very little depth and complexity. 
 Would I recommend this read? Of course! It's easy-going fun that doesn't require too much concentration. It's ridiculously funny in parts, and the incorporation of Greek Mythology into today's world is loads of fun to read about. Plus, it's a fast read, perfect for your next vacation. I'm starting the final book now and I'm looking forward to seeing how it ends. Happy reading!

Harry's bedroom is the tiny room under the stairs, meanwhile, Dudley has two bedrooms, one to sleep in and one for all of his toys! This is the life that Harry has lived for the past ten years. Then one day a letter arrives for him, but instead of being allowed to read it, his uncle keeps them from Harry. But there is no escape. The Battle Of The Labyrinth (Percy Jackson And The Olympians #4), by Rick Riordan 
 Synopsis: Percy Jackson isn't expecting freshman orientation to be any fun. But when a mysterious mortal acquaintance appears on campus, followed by demon cheerleaders, things quickly move from bad to worse. 
 In this fourth installment of the blockbuster series, time is running out as war between the Olympians and the evil Titan lord Kronos draws near. Even the safe haven of Camp Half-Blood grows more vulnerable by the minute as Kronos's army prepares to invade its once impenetrable borders.  My Thoughts: At this point I admit I'm starting to just power through the series. It's a fun series that kids and young adults would really enjoy, but as an adult I don't feel as wowed as I could be. The chapter titles still pull a chuckle out of me, and there are sentences peppered throughout the story that are also pretty funny (case in point: "You hit the Lord of the Titans in the eye with a blue plastic hairbrush"). The Battle Of The Labyrinth (Percy Jackson And The Olympians #4), by Rick Riordan 
 Synopsis: Percy Jackson isn't expecting freshman orientation to be any fun. But when a mysterious mortal acquaintance appears on campus, followed by demon cheerleaders, things quickly move from bad to worse. 
 In this fourth installment of the blockbuster series, time is running out as war between the Olympians and the evil Titan lord Kronos draws near. Even the safe haven of Camp Half-Blood grows more vulnerable by the minute as Kronos's army prepares to invade its once impenetrable borders.  In A Sentence: A decent read, but I'm not feeling very wowed by this series (not yet anyway) 
 My Thoughts: At this point I admit I'm starting to just power through the series. It's a fun series that kids and young adults would really enjoy, but as an adult I don't feel as wowed as I could be. It's ridiculously funny in parts, and the incorporation of Greek Mythology into today's world is loads of fun to read about. Plus, it's a fast read, perfect for your next vacation. Short and Sweet Review, by Michelle: 
 Ahh, all good things must come to an end. I am a Harry Potter nut. Why the three stars then? Well, I don't know to be honest with you. I "liked it", but I just don't know if I can go further than that. Maybe 3.5 stars? What really ruined the book for me was the epilogue. Had Ms. Rowling not included the epilogue, I think I could have gone with 4 stars. It just felt so cheesy after all the darkness that we've experienced throughout the development of the story. 
 Eh, well, I think that's all I really need to say. I highly doubt someone is scouring reviews of Harry Potter to decide if they're going to read it or not. ;) So I'll keep in short & sweet, per usual!

I think this book is a good representation of the series as a whole, charming characters, great story, and a setting that is very well crafted. I am sad that this series is over and I won't complain if more eventually are written (whether with old characters or a new generation or a mix of both) but if that happens or not I think this story's ending was absolutely perfect. I can't recommend this book and the series enough, it is just really incredible. 
 Just a quick note, Peeves has easily the best assist in the battle. (Wouldn't mind a Peeves prequel story, you know before being a ghost, just an idea...could be good...I mean really good)

A pesar de que fue el ultimo de la saga, y con el venia el final de la saga, lo ame. Ame la batalla, odie la muerte de Dobby, y...fue simplemente sorprendente. El mejor final de todos los tiempos, sin duda. 
 ALWAYS <3

This is the seventh and final book of the Harry Potter series. I loved this book. I thought it was well written and really fun to read. I wanted to read as quickly as I could but also slow down and enjoy it as it's the last one. When I finished, I felt like my best friend had left me. 
 This was one of the better books in the series. I love them all but this one tied up all the loose ends and really kept me enthralled. I was afraid that it would seem odd when I found out that Harry, Ron, and Hermione weren't going back to Hogwarts, but I was pleasantly surprised. Rowling kept the feel of "Harry Potter" throughout. 
 Some people were upset by the Epilogue, thinking that it was gratuitous. I can see where they are coming from but I, personally, enjoyed it. I thought it was nice to finally see Harry have a happy, normal ending. He spent the first 17 years of his life in an uproar, nothing was easy for him, he was constantly in danger. It was nice to know that, in the end, he lived a normal, calm life. 
 I thought this was a great ending to the series. It was highly suspenseful and entertaining. I loved it.

2017 reread. I remember being disappointed in this ending. It was worth 3 stars then, and I'm giving it 4 now. 
 I think the difference is me, and what point in life I read it. Some fundamental issues I had with the book were more about me, my life experiences at the time, and I was fairly exhausted and impatient generally in 2007. 
 For example, I hated the Dumbledore scenes, but now I don't. I hated the resolution, and now I don't. Maybe I've just had time to sit with the ideas, or maybe the straight through reread made it so much deeper for me. I'm not sure. 
 I still feel it's unevenly paced, and I do wish there had been equal time to the last half of the book as the first. I wish we could have seen more of Hogwarts, had a clue what was going on with DA and Snape. The wand stuff really seems spotty, still. But generally, it's a much more satisfying resolution to the story than I remember. 
 On to The Cursed Child!
I can't express how much I love this series. Storytelling at its best: good vs evil, friendship, redemption, self-denial, faithfulness, etc. Love it!

give me back my life damnit, I could have done without 500 pages of the book. Wish I had gone with my initial instinct and just checked for a detailed synopsis. Thank goodness for the couple of scenes that did end up finishing the series nicely, but give me lloyd alexander any day over this. The series would have been much better if 5,6, and 7 had been consolidated into one reasonably sized book.
